newsitem.title: USA: Ashland Coal holders okay merger deal.
newsitem.headline: Ashland Coal holders okay merger deal.

text.p: Ashland Coal Inc said Monday its stockholders had overwhelmingly approved the company's merger with Arch Mineral, a St. Louis-based marketer and transporter of bituminous coal.
Under the terms of the merger, Ashland Coal's common shareholders will receive one common share of the merged company, Arch Coal Inc, for each Ashland Coal share.
In January, Ashland Coal and Arch Mineral announced that their respective boards had agreed in principle to combine the two companies.

Ashland said the merger creates the sixth largest coal producer in the U.S. and the largest producer of low-sulfur coal in eastern United States. The merger will be effective on Tuesday, July 1, it said.

The merged entity will have annual revenues of about $1.3 billion from production of more than 50 million tons. It will have coal reserves of more than 2.0 billion tons and total assets of about $1.7 billion, it said.
Arch Coal will be a publicly traded company with 39.6 million shares outstanding and its stock will begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on July 1 under the symbol.
Both companies are partially owned by Ashland Inc which holds about 56 percent of Ashland Coal and about 50 percent of Arch Mineral.
The company's coal mines are in West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky, Illinois and Wyoming. Its market include electric utilities in the midwestern and eastern U.S. and buyers abroad.
